text:
St. Louis arrives at Nashville as the team that has controlled more of the play. At five on five the Blues have taken 53% of the expected goals this season to Nashville's 43%, and the model expects a close game, 3.1 to 2.85 for STL. The Blues create 3.26 expected goals per 60 and allow 3.03; the Predators sit at 2.75 and 3.14. Special teams lean Nashville's way: the Predators' power play generates 0.68 expected goals a game to STL's 0.48, and STL takes 4.1 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side chances with the man advantage. Both teams play on one day of rest.

Recent form tells a similar story. STL is 2-2-1 in its last five with 56% of the expected goals, winning the chance battle in three of them, including 5-3 and 7-2 wins before a 5-4 loss at Minnesota. NSH is 1-1-3 in its last five with 48% of the expected goals, and the Predators are winless in three (0-1-2), outscored 11-6. The chances say that slump is partly real, at 49% of the expected goals.

In net, projected starters Joel Hofer (STL) and Juuse Saros (NSH) are nearly identical this season, at +1.3 and +1.3 goals saved above expected. Last season separates them: Hofer was +11.05 over 46 games, Saros -10.19 over 59. Among players to watch, Mason McTavish (STL) is on a five-game point streak and has a 30% chance to score. For Nashville, Steven Stamkos (36%) and Filip Forsberg (35%) each have strong numbers against STL, with 7 and 6 points in 4 games. Pavel Buchnevich (STL) and Mavrik Bourque (NSH) are both day-to-day and could return.
